SMTO-GWT-0047 — A file copy stopped because its conversation or Task was deleted

GUID: f97d911f-a9dd-4f1b-905f-9084bcba6fc7
Slug: transfer-run-abandoned
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gwt

What happened

  • SMTO was copying a file between two computers, but the conversation or Task that started the copy was deleted, so SMTO stopped the copy. The file may or may not have reached its destination.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the computer you were copying to, open the destination folder and check whether the file is there and has the size you expect. SMTO stopped tracking the copy partway, so only the destination folder shows whether it finished.
  2. If the file is there and complete, leave it as it is and don't start another copy. Copying again could overwrite a file that already arrived correctly.
  3. If the file is missing or the wrong size, open a conversation that still exists, or select New chat, and ask SMTO to copy the file again. The deleted conversation can't continue the copy, but a new request starts a fresh copy that SMTO can track.

What success looks like

  • The file is in the destination folder with the expected size, and you only started a new copy if it was missing.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before trying it again. Select Copy error details and send them, with the source and destination file paths, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't try to restore the deleted conversation or Task to finish the old copy.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Transfer checkpoint persistence refused to update the gateway.copy receipt because the owning native run (or its conversation, journal or originating request) has been deleted (tombstoned).

What this means

  • Transfer checkpoint persistence found the owning run tombstoned and refused to update that abandoned run's receipt. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Transfer checkpoint persistence found the owning run tombstoned and refused to update that abandoned run's receipt.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the run's abandonment state, original transfer receipt and any staged or published destination data.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the destination path on the destination Gateway (existence, size, revision or SHA-256) and any leftover staging against the transfer's last recorded phase: a failure before the committing phase triggers destination_abort, while a failure after commit can leave a fully published file. Start a new gateway.copy from a live conversation only for files that are still missing or wrong; do not try to revive the deleted run.
  • Inspect transfer receipts and any staged content through the existing recovery flow. Start new work only for the changes still required.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Existing transfer effects are reconciled and any remaining work has a separately authorized live owner.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
